Test a robust trimmed‑mean over the full pool to see if trimming outliers improves the already strong weighted result, motivated by the high trend and strong seasonality but unstable ranking.
test a weighted combination with softmax_neg_error to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over trimmed mean given strong trend/seasonality but unstable rankings.
The series has high trend and seasonality but unstable rankings; a robust median may reduce influence of outliers and correlated errors.
Try a dba combination on a smaller, diverse pool (pool1) to see if a more aggressive aggregation improves robustness given unstable rankings.
Test a weighted combination on the smaller, high‑rank pool1 using inverse_error weights to see if focusing on the top performers improves over the current dba result.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable ranking; a simple mean over the smaller, more stable pool1 (ARIMA, ETS, THETA, catboost, DWT_rf) may capture diverse signals without overfitting.
test a softmax_neg_error weighted combo on the compact pool1 to see if emphasizing low-error models improves over dba.
The series has strong trend/seasonality and unstable rankings; a robust DBA over the full pool may outperform previous DBA on pool1.
Test a weighted combination on the expanded pool2 (adding FT_rf) using inverse_error to see if including the best recent model improves over pool1 weighted results.

Test a weighted combination over the full pool using the w1 handle to see if a different weighting scheme on all models improves over the current leader, given the high trend and seasonality but unstable rankings.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool2 weighted by w6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.865. Series context: trend strength 0.9544 and seasonal strength 0.6993; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.228); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.623.
